author: Greenjungle
quote:
All Graphics, Zero Soul
You can buy out the gaming media and flood user scores with brand-new bot accounts dropping 10/10s, but you can’t fool longtime players. Aside from the graphics, this game is a massive disappointment that strips away everything that ever gave GTA its soul.
​Going from iconic leads like Michael, Trevor, and Franklin—or the energy of San Andreas—to Jason and Lucia is a brutal downgrade. Both leads are painfully unlikable, and Lucia in particular is grating; half the time it doesn't feel like a crime epic, it feels like a chore simulator where you're just running errands to keep her happy. The writing fell off a cliff. Instead of sharp satire, it’s sterile, safe, and full of cringe dialogue that makes you want to skip cutscenes on your very first playthrough.
​Worse, the gameplay itself feels neutered. For an open-world criminal sandbox, there are somehow more things you can’t do than can. You can’t even hijack any car you want anymore, and any actual shady activity feels heavily sanitized and committee-approved. The missions are dull, heavily railroaded with zero meaningful plot choices, and buried under unskippable filler that wastes your time between the rare fun moments.
​Even the basics took a step backward. Driving feels noticeably worse than it did in GTA 5, and watching the framerate dip under 30 FPS on PS5 during big action set-pieces in 2026—right when performance matters most—is completely unacceptable.
​Whatever regime changes happened behind the scenes at Rockstar and Take-Two clearly gutted the studio. They took the edge, freedom, and bite out of Grand Theft Auto and left behind a pretty, hollow shell. Save your money.
